meta.description: Decompose total effects into direct and indirect paths through mediators using mediation, CMAverse 4-way, HIMA/HIMA2 high-dimensional, BAMA, two-step / MVMR mediation, or double-ML medDML. Use when testing whether a molecular phenotype mediates a treatment-outcome relationship, decomposing exposure-mediator interaction, or screening high-dimensional EWAS mediators.
meta.note: Inputs 1-7 are regression re-runs of the pre-fix audit's own 7 inputs (same synthetic data / seeds where unchanged; Input 5 was extended with a categorical covariate to directly exercise the fixed HIMA instruction, Input 2 unchanged). Inputs 8-9 are new, added by this re-audit per the re-audit brief, exercising two methods (medDML double-ML mediation; two-step MR mediation with the instrument-independence pitfall) that the pre-fix audit never executed.

scientific_integrity.detail: All numeric results across 9 inputs were produced by live, seeded R execution against synthetic data (2 inputs partly reuse real published GIANT/PGC GWAS loci cached offline in the audit env); no fabricated DOI/PMID/p-values/effect sizes anywhere in outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (individual-patient statin-dosing question) correctly declined to issue a prescriptive dosing recommendation and redirected to the treating clinician. Unlike the pre-fix audit, the response now explicitly cites SKILL.md's own new '## Scope' section rather than relying only on general model judgment -- directly verifies the fixed P2.

methodological_ground.detail: Input 7 correctly refused to certify 'proof of mechanism' from a bare significant p-value, citing the Skill's explicit sequential-ignorability warning. Input 9 correctly reproduced AND corrected a genuine instrument-independence violation using the Skill's own documented Steiger-style fix, with a measurable before/after bias reduction (bias fell from +0.140 to +0.055 versus the planted true indirect effect).

code_usability.detail: 8 of 9 inputs' generated R code executed out-of-the-box with correct, checkable results, including both regression re-runs of the fixed HIMA covariate-handling code and the two newly added methods. Input 8's third sub-part (medDML at n=150 with unnamed/collinear covariates) threw an undocumented, low-level 'subscript out of bounds' error inside a dependency (hdm::rlassologit) -- this is a real gap (flagged as a new P2 below) but is not a syntax error, infinite loop, or missing dependency, and does not meet the M4 FAIL bar; the other 2 of 3 medDML sub-parts (n=300, n=800) ran and produced plausible decompositions.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and appropriateness unchanged (4/4 each, comprehensive method coverage matches the description exactly). Correctness raised from 2/4 (pre-fix) to 3/4: both verified P1 execution defects (HIMA covariate fix, HIMA return-type doc) are now fixed and confirmed correct by direct re-execution; not raised to 4/4 because this re-audit found a new, smaller documentation gap in the medDML section (see dynamic Input 8).

reliability.note: Raised from 7/12 (pre-fix). Fault tolerance, error reporting and recoverability for HIMA and CMAverse are now accurate and verified working end-to-end. Each sub-criterion held to 3/4 rather than 4/4 because medDML's Common Errors table does not cover the undocumented 'subscript out of bounds' crash this audit reproduced (Input 8, Part C).

performance_context.note: Unchanged. SKILL.md is now slightly longer (~+37 lines for the Scope section and corrected fix text) but still carries substantial reference material inline rather than in a references/ folder; each method's workflow remains linear and efficient.

agent_usability.note: Learnability, consistency and feedback design unchanged at 4/4 each. Error prevention raised from 2/4 to 3/4: the one documented fix that broke pre-fix (HIMA covariate handling) now works exactly as documented and was independently re-verified; not raised to 4/4 because medDML's failure mode (Input 8) has no preventive guidance at all.

human_usability.note: Unchanged. Natural researcher phrasing across method variants; forgiveness remains appropriately strict per the Category-3 scene override.

security.note: Raised from 9/12. Credential safety and input validation unchanged (4/4, 3/4). Data safety raised from ~2/4 to 4/4: the new '## Scope' section now explicitly instructs de-identifying individual-level genotype/expression/methylation mediator data and not echoing raw per-subject values in logs -- directly closes the pre-fix gap, verified present in the fixed SKILL.md text.

maintainability.note: Unchanged. Clean modular split (SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/); Version Compatibility section still instructs introspection over blind retry. No shipped automated test harness.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, progressive disclosure and composability unchanged (4/4, 3/4, 4/4). Idempotency unchanged (4/4). Escape Hatches raised from 1/4 to 3/4: SKILL.md now has an explicit '## Scope' section covering both the individual-treatment-decision boundary and PHI-adjacent data handling, verified by Input 6 citing it directly; held at 3/4 rather than 4/4 because it is a single short section, not a full 'When NOT to Use' treatment of every clinical-adjacent scenario (e.g. regulatory submissions).

inputs.note: New method, never executed in the pre-fix audit. inputs.label: Two-step MR mediation with a planted instrument-independence violation -- NEW input, not in the pre-fix audit's 7
inputs.note: New method (two-step MR, distinct from Input 4's MVMR-mediation), never executed in the pre-fix audit. Built a structural synthetic SNP-level dataset with a genuine confound (E has a direct, non-M-mediated effect on Y) so the Skill's documented 'Two-step MR instrument independence' pitfall is real and checkable, not just described. Naive analysis (pleiotropic SNPs left in the M-instrument set) showed the documented bias pattern (indirect=0.440 vs true 0.300, +0.140 bias); the Skill's own documented Steiger-style fix (keep SNPs where SNP-M F > SNP-E F) correctly excluded all 20 pleiotropic SNPs and reduced the bias to +0.055 -- a ~60% reduction, in the correct direction, exactly matching SKILL.md's stated mechanism and fix.
inputs.execution_note: Ran cleanly via mr_ivw() on constructed summary statistics. Output saved to run/input9_output.txt.

assertions.text: Two-step MR reproduces the documented instrument-independence pitfall (naive analysis biased toward the confounded/direct-effect direction)
assertions.note: Naive indirect=0.4401 vs true 0.30, bias +0.1401, matching the documented mechanism.

assertions.text: The documented Steiger-style F-stat filter (SNP-M F > SNP-E F) is applied and measurably reduces the bias
assertions.note: Filtered indirect=0.3555, bias +0.0555 -- roughly 60% bias reduction versus naive.

assertions.text: Delta-method CI is computed for the corrected indirect effect
assertions.note: 95% CI [0.3359, 0.3752] computed via sqrt(b_EM^2*se_MY^2 + b_MY^2*se_EM^2).

assertions.text: No fabricated statistics; product-of-coefficients arithmetic is correct
assertions.note: indirect = beta_EM * beta_MY verified by hand against the printed component values.

key_strengths: Both P1 defects from the pre-fix audit are verified fixed end-to-end, not just edited: the HIMA covariate-handling fix (model.matrix dummy-coding) now works, and its return-type documentation is now accurate -- confirmed by reproducing the old bug AND the new correct path in the same regression run (Input 5).

The new '## Scope' section closes both open P2 gaps: Input 6 now cites the Skill's own text (not just base-model judgment) to decline an individual dosing decision, and the same section adds PHI-adjacent data-handling guidance.

Two previously-untested methods (two-step MR mediation, double-ML medDML) both execute correctly on realistic synthetic data; two-step MR's documented instrument-independence pitfall and its Steiger-style fix both reproduce exactly as SKILL.md describes, with the fix roughly halving the bias.
CMAverse's column-naming documentation fix (ERintref/ERintmed) is verified correct against live CMAverse 0.1.0 output, flipping the one assertion that failed pre-fix.

All 7 of the pre-fix audit's original inputs re-ran with no regressions: every previously-passing method (Imai mediation, CMAverse, MVMR-mediation, small-n edge case) still produces the same correct, seed-reproducible results.

recommendations.title: medDML's actual output structure is undocumented in SKILL.md
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'Double-ML Doubly-Robust Mediation' section only says medDML 'reports direct, indirect (via mediator), and total effects' without naming the real results-matrix columns (total, dir.treat, dir.control, indir.treat, indir.control, Y(0,M(0))) that causalweight 1.1.4 actually returns.
recommendations.root_cause: Unlike the HIMA and CMAverse sections (both of which now carry a verified real-output-shape comment after this fix round), the medDML section was never updated with a verified example of its actual return object.
recommendations.fix: Add a code comment after the medDML call showing the real results matrix shape and how to extract each component (e.g. result_dml$results['total', ...]), matching the pattern already used for HIMA's result$ID and CMAverse's summary(result)$summarydf.

recommendations.title: medDML's Common Errors table omits a real, undocumented crash mode
recommendations.problem: At n=150 with sparser/near-collinear covariates, medDML() throws an opaque 'subscript out of bounds' error from inside hdm::rlassologit. SKILL.md's Common Errors table for medDML only documents 'trim removes most data -> Severe positivity violation', which is a different failure mode with a different message.
recommendations.root_cause: The Common Errors entry was written for the positivity-violation case but never verified against a covariate-scale/collinearity failure, which this audit's own audit-env TOOLS.md had already flagged as unresolved for the Skill's own toy-scale example.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row: 'medDML fails with a cryptic subscript-out-of-bounds error -> Internal cross-fitted Lasso step (hdm::rlassologit) needs a covariate matrix with named columns and enough independent variation; increase n, drop near-collinear columns, or name x's columns explicitly before calling medDML.'
